Cc: finance@clearcapmed.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected Jan usage spike — request for reconciliation

Hi Neha,

Hope you’re well. We pulled our January consumption and noticed a significant retroactive spike between Jan 8–20 that appears to have been billed to our committed capacity. The attached CSV shows the hourly token counts and a couple of example requests that look like long-running inference jobs.

Can you help reconcile what caused the overage and confirm whether there’s a path to a one-time offset? We’re in renewal conversations and want to get the books clean before the contract amendment.

Attached: usage_report_jan2026.csv

Thanks,
Emma Thomas

Subject: Re: Unexpected Jan usage spike — request for reconciliation

Hi Emma — thanks for the heads up and for sending the CSV. I opened a quick review with our billing and infra teams to trace the spike. A few quick notes:

- We’ll validate the per-request traces against our KV-cache and batch logs to confirm whether these were legitimate user-driven requests or a replay/batch misconfiguration.
- If the consumption is confirmed to be non-customer-triggered (platform retry/replay), we typically propose a one-time credit and reissue a corrected invoice.
- If it’s customer-initiated but outside the committed profile, we can propose a true-up invoice and discuss a discounted top-up as part of your renewal.

I’d like to propose a 30-minute call Thurs 2/19 to walk through the attachments and agree next steps. Are you available 9am PT / 12pm ET?

I’ll loop Ben (billing) and Marissa (renewals) to expedite reconciliation.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected Jan usage spike — request for reconciliation

Ben / Marissa — forwarding ClearCap’s raw report (attached) — they’re asking for a reconciliation and a one-time offset ahead of renewal. Quick context: ClearCap is evaluating a committed + burst increase as part of the renewal; resolving this cleanly will help close the amendment.

Please validate:
1) Match the rows in usage_report_jan2026.csv to our token logs (hourly granularity).
2) Identify any platform-side replays/retries or long-lived inference sessions (KV/cache hits) that would suggest non-user-caused consumption.
3) Provide a recommended settlement (credit USD and/or token offset) and draft language we can send to the customer.

Target: get a proposal ready by EOD Wed so I can share it on the 2/19 call.

Thanks,
Neha

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:36:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected Jan usage spike — request for reconciliation

Neha / Marissa — I pulled the token-level audit and infra traces. Summary:

- We matched 92% of the rows in their CSV to valid customer requests originating from their API key. 8% (~36k tokens) are anomalous: repeated long sequences that line up with a scheduled job we show as retried during Jan 12–14. The retries were triggered by a transient GPU preemption in one of the Dedicated pools that day.
- Financial impact: the anomalous 8% nets to $1,650 in overage at their current unit rates.

Recommendation: propose a one-time goodwill credit of $1,200 (cover ~73% of the anomaly) and reissue an adjusted invoice for the remaining $450. Also offer a one-time token rollover of 50k tokens toward the renewal burst pool as a customer success gesture.

Attached: audit_log_summary.pdf (redacted request ids).

If you want, I can draft the invoice and the short settlement note for Emma.

—Ben
Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@clearcapmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, finance@clearcapmed.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Jan usage spike — reconciliation & settlement proposal

Hi Emma — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary and proposed settlement below.

Summary of findings (Redwood audit):
- Date range reviewed: 2026-01-08 through 2026-01-20
- Matched customer-initiated usage: 92%
- Anomalous/replayed consumption likely caused by transient GPU preemption and automated retries: ~8% (~36,120 tokens)
- Gross overage amount (before adjustments): $1,650

Proposed settlement:
- One-time goodwill credit: $1,200 applied to your Feb invoice
- Adjusted invoice for remaining balance: $450 (attached PDF)
- One-time token rollover: 50,000 tokens credited to your renewal burst pool (no cash value)

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the settlement in reply to this thread.
2) If accepted, we’ll reissue the adjusted invoice and provide a DocuSign link for the invoice acknowledgment. The adjusted invoice is attached (ClearCap_updated_invoice_FEB2026.pdf).
3) We’ll apply the token rollover the day the renewed commitment is signed (or immediately if you prefer a provisional credit — let me know).

If you’d like a short handoff call to run through the audit, Ben and I are available tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks again for working through this — we appreciate the partnership and will make sure this is captured cleanly in the renewal amendment.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Success Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0411

Attachments: ClearCap_updated_invoice_FEB2026.pdf
